entities.summary: Jayavarman VI, a 12th-century Khmer monarch, ruled the Khmer Empire from 1100 to 1107, playing a pivotal role in the medieval era. He expanded the empire's borders, established new trade routes, and fostered cultural exchange with neighboring kingdoms. His reign saw the construction of temples, including the magnificent Preah Khan temple, which remains a testament to his architectural and artistic vision. Jayavarman VI's legacy extends beyond his own empire, as his policies and achievements influenced the development of Southeast Asian kingdoms and the rise of Hinduism in the region. As the Khmer Empire began to decline, Jayavarman VI's successors continued to build upon his foundations, ensuring his impact on the region's history was lasting. The inscription on his temple, which records his military campaigns and administrative reforms, remains one of the most well-preserved examples of medieval Khmer script.
